title: SFA vs TexasAM: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: Stephen F Austin State University (SFA) versus University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (TexasAM). Also searched as TexasAM vs SFA. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: Stephen F Austin State University (SFA) and University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (TexasAM) are both public institutions located in Texas, but they differ in several key aspects. SFA is situated in Nacogdoches and has an undergraduate enrollment of 8,728 students, whereas TexasAM is located in Dallas and does not report undergraduate enrollment figures. Additionally, SFA's in-state tuition is $11,128, while TexasAM's tuition information is not specified. These differences highlight the distinct profiles of the two universities in terms of size, location, and tuition costs.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: Stephen F Austin State University (SFA) and University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (TexasAM) differ notably in their cost structures. SFA charges an in-state tuition of $11,128 and an out-of-state tuition of $23,426. In contrast, TexasAM does not publicly specify its tuition rates for either in-state or out-of-state students. Regarding student debt, the median debt for completers at SFA is $23,409, while TexasAM does not provide this data. These financial figures illustrate the available cost information for SFA compared to the limited data from TexasAM.

When comparing SFA vs TexasAM, it is evident that SFA offers transparent tuition and debt statistics, which can aid prospective students in financial planning. TexasAM's lack of disclosed tuition and median debt figures makes direct cost comparisons challenging. Nonetheless, SFA's tuition rates and median debt provide a clear picture of the financial commitment required for attendance.

sections.heading: Learning model and campus
paragraphs: Stephen F Austin State University (SFA) and University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (TexasAM) differ in their learning models and campus settings. SFA, located in Nacogdoches, Texas, serves an undergraduate population of 8,728 students, indicating a traditional university structure with a focus on undergraduate education. In contrast, TexasAM is based in Dallas, Texas, and does not report undergraduate enrollment, reflecting its specialized role as a medical center primarily focused on graduate and professional education. The urban setting of TexasAM contrasts with SFA's smaller city environment, which may influence the campus experience and learning atmosphere.

When comparing SFA vs TexasAM, the distinction in campus locations and student populations highlights their differing educational missions. SFA's larger undergraduate enrollment suggests a broader range of undergraduate programs, while TexasAM's absence of undergraduate data aligns with its emphasis on medical and health sciences education. These factors contribute to unique learning environments tailored to their respective institutional goals.
